30 A fine mist of oil droplets is sprayed into air. As the oil droplets leave the nozzle of the spraying
device they can become electrically charged.
What is not a possible value for the charge on an oil droplet?
A
zero
B
1.0 × 10–19
C
C
4.8 × 10–19
C
D
8.0 × 10–19
C

hints: Notice the four charge values in $\text{C}$ and ask whether each can be built from whole electrons gained or lost by the oil droplet.
Recall charge is quantised as $Q = ne$ where $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $n$ must be a whole number including zero.
Divide each non-zero value such as $4.8 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $8.0 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ by $1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and check which division does not give a whole number.
walkthrough: Identify the rule tested: free charge exists in whole multiples of the elementary charge, $Q = ne$, because charging is gain or loss of whole electrons.
Recall $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and that $n = 0, \pm 1, \pm 2...$ is allowed, so zero charge is possible for a neutral droplet.
Test each value by calculating $n = Q/e$. For $4.8 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, $n = 4.8/1.6 = 3$. For $8.0 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, $n = 8.0/1.6 = 5$.
For $1.0 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, $n = 1.0/1.6 = 0.625$, which is not a whole number and is also smaller than one $e$.
Therefore only $1.0 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ cannot be formed from whole electrons. This is option B.

A.explanation: Zero means no net excess of electrons or protons, which is allowed as $n = 0$ in $Q = ne$.

B.explanation: This is less than one elementary charge and is not a whole multiple of $1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, so it cannot occur by gain or loss of electrons.

C.explanation: This equals $3 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, so it is three elementary charges and is allowed.

D.explanation: This equals $5 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, so it is five elementary charges and is allowed.
